title: What implements sandboxed execution, and which tier first?
statement: REQ-0005 requires claims to be testable by execution in a real environment. #56 decides three tiers and #77 decides how they activate, but no controller exists for any of them. Which tier is built first, and what provisions, executes, observes and destroys?
notes: BLOCKING under DEC-0002. BOUNDARIES BEFORE MECHANISM (DEC-0003): (a) what may execute; (b) filesystem/network/credential boundaries per tier (#56) and what a tier may NOT reach; (c) resource limits — time, cost, instance count — since #77's authorisation is meaningless without them; (d) cleanup via #56's `destroy`, and what happens when it fails; (e) ⚠️ AN EVIDENCE-SURVIVAL CONTRACT (#122). What survives a run: environment facts, tool and runtime VERSIONS, inputs, outputs, exit status, timing, permission denials, and explicit omission or redaction reasons. ⚠️ Stated precisely: an absent fact does NOT make the record inapplicable. It stays applicable with an `unknown` comparison; what the absence changes is the attainable RUNG, capping it below environment-matched. So a silent omission decides how strong a claim can ever become, invisibly. ⚠️ And the recorded states describe the OBSERVER, never relevance. Relevance is claim-relative (#105) — the same record may be decisive for another assertion — so `not relevant` is not something evidence can hold. The honest states are: not captured · not observable · unavailable · redacted, with a reason. The applicability layer decides whether the gap matters to a given claim. ⚠️ Which of those states to declare is part of THIS question, because only the states a sandbox can genuinely DETECT are worth declaring — declaring one nothing can distinguish repeats #121's error of promising a capability the host cannot check. Only after all of this does 'which tier first, implemented how' become answerable. ⚠️ AND THE FIELD'S SHAPE IS GOVERNED BY #123: evidence stores observations and provenance, never what they mean for a claim. So whatever this question settles must record why the OBSERVER lacks a fact, and must not smuggle in polarity, relevance, applicability, verdict or confidence — all of which are derived per claim and would be wrong the moment a second assertion cited the same record.
answer: Tier 1 first, behind a typed validation controller owning provision -> execute -> observe -> destroy, refusing jobs above the approved ceiling before provisioning. Jobs are declared (tier, inputs, argument-array commands, capture plan, limits, expected outputs, network/credential/cost needs); the specialist never gets a shell. Tier 1 is a temp workspace plus a Python venv, which isolates dependencies and is NOT an OS security sandbox — so it makes no containment, filesystem or network-isolation claim, and claims needing those require a higher tier. Every run yields an observation record whose capture plan makes omissions detectable: not captured / not observable / unavailable / redacted, each with a reason. Cleanup failure is a first-class result: keep the evidence, report the retained path. See DEC-0005.
